chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abī Ayyūb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, while I was with him, about the qunūt on the Day of Jumuʿah, so he said: In the second rakʿah.

He said to him: Some of our companions have narrated to us that you said: In the first rakʿah. So he said: In the last one. There were many people with him, so when he saw their heedlessness, he said: O Abā Muḥammad, in the first and the last.

He said: I said, May I be your ransom, before the rukūʿ or after it? He said: Every qunūt is before the rukūʿ except Jumuʿah; for in the first rakʿah the qunūt in it is before the rukūʿ, and in the last it is after the rukūʿ.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ: the second rakʿah of the prayer
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى: the first rakʿah of the prayer
key_terms.الْأَخِيرَةِ: the last rakʿah, meaning the second rakʿah in Jumuʿah prayer
key_terms.الْقُنُوتِ: the qunūt supplication performed in salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ: the Day of Jumuʿah, referring here to Friday and its prayer

ai.seo_question: Where is the qunūt performed in Salat al-Jumuʿah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling of qunūt in Salat al-Jumuʿah. It indicates that Jumuʿah prayer has two qunūts: one in the first rakʿah before rukūʿ, and one in the second rakʿah after rukūʿ. It also distinguishes this from the general rule that qunūt is ordinarily performed before rukūʿ.
